prompt_en: An intimate photograph creates a coherent complex photographic scene with a woman whose visible face and hair follow the supplied reference image, absorbed in one connected moment of everyday activity: restoring the lifted ribbon on the same supported hat at the existing seated work surface. Use the reference for facial contours, dark eyes, natural pink lips and the dark chin-length bob with wispy fringe. Her calm, attentive presence and natural skin texture carry the portrait as she leans slightly toward the small repair. A close, gently elevated front three-quarter camera frames her face, both shoulder-to-forearm chains, both complete working hands, the hat and the nearer turned jacket cuff together in one horizontal photograph. The working hands sit close to the face's plane, and the nearer cuff presents a broad flat patch in the lower-left foreground. The woman holds the sewing needle between her right thumb and index finger while her left fingertips pin the ribbon to the hat beside the fresh stitch. The sewing needle has one metallic shaft, a pointed tip and a clearly exposed eye threaded with golden thread. At this shutter moment the needle has emerged from the ribbon. Her right thumb and index make a small sideways pinch on the middle of the shaft. The needle lies almost horizontally across the picture: its sharp point projects freely to the left of the pinch, while the open threaded eye projects freely to the right. A visible length of silver shaft extends on each side of the fingertip pads, clearly separating both exposed endpoints from the holding fingers. One continuous length of golden thread passes through that eye and runs in a simple unobstructed curve to the fresh stitch in the exposed ribbon immediately beside her left pinning fingertips. The gold thread is a fine line distinctly separate from the silver shaft. The lifted loose portion of the ribbon and the short newly secured portion belong to that same hat, so her careful action and its useful result can be read together. The nearer turned jacket cuff belongs to her working right wrist. Its broad exposed surface is thin flat woven cloth, with a neatly folded edge followed by a separate continuous row of small sewing stitches. Fine interlaced yarns remain visible across the same textile surface beside its stitched edge. Fine straight warp and weft strands cross at right angles, with tiny over-and-under intersections clearly distinguishable directly beside the sewn stitch row on this same cuff patch. The woven surface and its sewn edge face the camera together; the flat patch occupies enough of the close foreground for those crossings and individual sewing stitches to resolve. Her bent elbows keep both hands close together above the supported hat, and her seated torso rests comfortably behind the surface. The fingertips, both free needle ends, threaded eye, whole gold curve, fresh ribbon stitch and broad cuff patch have separate visible contours within a shared clear plane. The chair back and edge of the work surface retain enough form to identify the seated repair setting behind her. Side window light grazes the cuff's yarn intersections, its stitch row and the silver needle, making their small natural shadows and metallic glints visible. The face rests above the quiet center formed by the working hands, while the supported hat fills the lower part of the frame. Moderate depth of field keeps the eyes, acting hands, needle endpoints, thread connection and cuff crossings crisp together, with the existing place cue softly identifiable. Render the connected moment with restrained documentary intimacy, believable proportions, continuous fingers and wrists, realistic thread thickness and the tactile clarity of an actual close photograph. One shared focus zone keeps the recognizable face, the needle-gripping hand with its ribbon contact, and the softly legible chair and work-surface edge connected in the photograph.
